research_outcome: BOUNDED_SUPPORTED — unfree household/slavery is supportable in grand-ducal court structures around the 1300 horizon; polity-wide prevalence, uniform status law and later-serfdom continuity are not established
bounded_proposition: Late-thirteenth/fourteenth-century grand-ducal court structures in Lithuanian lands included a separately identified unfree household/slave population (nelaisvoji šeimyna; vergai; šeimynykščiai), with captives among sources of that population.
required_abstention: Do not infer whole-polity prevalence, uniform law, universal household slaveholding, captive=slave automatically, ordinary dues=slavery, later serfdom at 1300, or any practice polygon.
evidence_locus: Grand-ducal court/valsčius structures in Lithuanian lands; near-anchor Lithuanian external raiding/capture retained separately as context.
inference_extent: Institutional presence in at least part of the grand-ducal domain/court economy around 1300; not uniform across all GDL territories.
law_practice_note: No exact 1300 slave statute recovered; later 1529 statutory categories and mature serfdom are temporal controls only and are not back-projected.
network_territorial_note: Near-anchor raids show capture/forced movement outside the polity; external capture is not substituted for territorial slave status. Territorial support comes from the distinct grand-ducal court unfree-household reconstruction.
category_mapping_note: Unfree household/slave terminology is preserved; categories are related but not flattened into one universal chattel-slavery or serfdom class.
language_access_limitations: Core specialist evidence is Lithuanian; Jeroschin is Middle High German accessed in Mary Fischer's English translation. Jurginis 1960 was bibliographically recovered but not read in full.
geometry_claim_role: Navigation/identity context only; not evidence of slavery extent.
geometry_unresolved_note: Changing polity extent and uneven grand-ducal domain structures cannot define practice extent; no slavery polygon authorized.
